subject: Implementation MAP & evaluation cadence — Crestline Health
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@crestlinehealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Marco Santos <marco.santos@crestlinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-signature: MAP + constraints (first pass)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for a smooth signing call yesterday — excited to get started. Attached is a small constraints doc from our infra and security teams (Crestline-implementation-constraints.pdf). To move toward an internal launch decision, we need a mutual action plan that embeds: an evaluation plan (specific eval prompts & acceptance criteria), a canary rollout window, migration cutover steps for our existing bot, and training dates for two cohorts (ops + nurses).

High-level asks from our side:
- Canary: 2-week live canary limited to one region and 10% traffic
- Eval criteria: latency P95 < 800ms, hallucination rate < 2% on sampled clinical prompts, and token-accuracy on structured outputs > 98%
- Training: two 90-minute sessions (recorded), plus a train-the-trainer 45-minute session

Can you share a draft MAP that includes these items and a proposed close timeline? If we can get a working draft this week, procurement can align payment milestones.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Clinical Automation
Crestline Health

Attachment: Crestline-implementation-constraints.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-signature: MAP + constraints (first pass)

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and the constraints doc. Attaching our working MAP (redwood-map-draft.xlsx) — core sections include canary gating, eval harness, migration checklist, training curriculum, and acceptance milestones mapped to invoices.

Quick summary of the proposed cadence:
1) Week 0 (this week): Agreement on acceptance criteria + sign-off on MAP
2) Week 1–2: Pre-canary validation (offline evals against Crestline prompt set)
3) Week 3–4: Canary (10% traffic in East region) with daily health gates + mid-canary emergency rollback point
4) Week 5: Full migration cutover (nighttime maintenance window) + immediate smoke tests
5) Week 6: Training cohort 1 (ops) + train-the-trainer
6) Week 7: Training cohort 2 (nurses) + go/no-go review

Questions for you / needed items:
- Final list of evaluation prompts and a labeled validation set (can be redacted)
- Preferred maintenance window for cutover (we usually recommend 02:00–04:00 local)
- Any extra compliance gates (e.g., additional logging retention beyond default)

I’ve looped in Laura (Customer Success) to drive the day-to-day timeline and Marissa for the implementation playbook. Karthik will own the canary engineering plan and rollback scripting.

Next steps: Laura will send a detailed milestone board and meeting invites for the validation runbook. If that looks good, can we lock a provisional cutover date of July 7–8?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-map-draft.xlsx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 08:57:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation MAP & evaluation cadence — Crestline Health

Elena, Vivek — adding the implementation cadence and gating details below. I put more granular checkpoints into the shared Drive folder (link sent by Vivek).

Canary gating (daily checklist):
- Day 0 baseline: deploy model variant v1.0 to canary subpool; run smoke on 50 synthetic prompts
- Daily health checks (automated): P95 latency, error rate, token-consumption anomaly detection
- Manual QA: 30 sampled clinical prompts reviewed by Crestline SME (daily closeout)
- Gate to increase traffic: if all automated checks green and SME observations <= 1 critical issue, increase traffic by 2x (cap at 10%)
- Mid-canary hold point (end of Week 1 of canary): formal go/no-go review; rollback if hallucination metric > 2% or P95 > 900ms

Migration cutover checklist (night-of):
- Pre-cutover: freeze schema and lock integrations (30 mins prior)
- Cutover window: 02:00–03:30 local; execute traffic switch script; run smoke and acceptance batch; escalate to on-call infra if token mismatch or error > 0.5%
- Post-cutover: 4-hour elevated monitoring, then de-escalate to standard SLO cadence

Training schedule (live + recorded):
- Train-the-trainer: July 12, 09:00–09:45 PDT (virtual)
- Cohort 1 (ops): July 15, 10:00–11:30 PDT
- Cohort 2 (clinical): July 18, 13:00–14:30 PDT

I attached a first-pass training plan (training-plan-v1.docx) with session objectives and slide owners. Marissa will coordinate materials.

Laura Bennett
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marco Santos <marco.santos@crestlinehealth.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Implementation MAP & evaluation cadence — Crestline Health

Marco / Elena — thanks for surfacing procurement items. Proposed responses and updates to the MAP below. I will update the redwood-map-draft.xlsx and HubSpot deal record after we align.

Answers / proposal:
1) Invoice milestones: we propose milestone payments tied to (A) MAP sign-off, (B) successful canary completion (as defined by the eval pass), and (C) post-cutover stability (30 days). If a canary is rolled back due to a Redwood defect, we will not invoice the canary milestone and will schedule remediation immediately. If the rollback is due to Crestline-chosen config change during canary, we will treat it as a contractual re-run and invoice per the timeline agreed in section 6.2 of the MAP.
2) Acceptance signer: final evaluation sign-off will be dual-signed — Crestline clinical lead (or their designee) and Redwood SME. This ensures both operational and clinical acceptance.
3) SLA credit: we can add a one-time, mutually capped SLA credit clause for the first 30 days post-cutover. Details: credit equal to 5% of the monthly invoice for P95 breaches > 20% above threshold, capped at the canary milestone invoice. Legal can draft language for the SOW addendum.

Next steps (this weekend):
- I’ll upload a revised MAP with the updated milestone language and acceptance table.
- Laura will set the validation-runbook workshop for Monday (2028-06-26).
- Marissa will prepare the training materials and a participant list template for your SMEs.

If that aligns, please confirm and we’ll lock dates.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference
